metadata.title: Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis with Compensated Cirrhosis: Developing Drugs for Treatment Guidance for Industry
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 34 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 35 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 36 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 37 not required. 38
candidates.context: 1 This guidance has been prepared by the Division of Gastroenterology and Inborn Error Products in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research at the Food and Drug Administration.

candidates.statement: Sponsors of drugs to treat compensated NASH cirrhosis should consider the following when 64 enrolling patients in phase 3 clinical trials: 65
candidates.context: A. Patient Population/Enrollment Criteria 62 • Sponsors should be careful to enroll in clinical trials only patients whose cirrhosis is 67 secondary to NASH and not caused by other etiologies. Patients should have histological 68 diagnoses of NASH, and other causes of chronic liver disease should be ruled out (e.g., 69 alcoholic liver disease, viral hepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, primary sclerosing 70 cholangitis, autoimmune hepatitis, Wilson’s disease, hemochromatosis, alpha-1- 71 antitrypsin deficiency, HIV). 72

candidates.statement: • Some patients with compensated NASH cirrhosis can be treated with vitamin E or 106 pioglitazone. Such patients should either (1) discontinue vitamin E or pioglitazone or (2) 107 be on a stable dose for 6 months before trial enrollment, and the dose should be held 108 constant during the trial. 109
candidates.context: • Sponsors can enroll patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) if they are adequately 102 controlled on a stable dose or doses of antidiabetic medication(s) for at least 3 months 103 before trial enrollment. 104 • Elevations of liver enzymes such as alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate 111 aminotransferase (AST) can be expected in NASH. However, ALT or AST elevation 112 greater than 5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN) would indicate the possibility of 113 concomitant liver disease(s) (e.g., alcohol-associated liver disease, autoimmune 114 hepatitis). Therefore, sponsors should not enroll patients with evidence of such 115 transaminase elevations. Similarly, bilirubin levels should not exceed ULN. Alkaline 116 phosphate should be less than 1.5 times the ULN. 117

candidates.statement: Sponsors of drugs to treat compensated NASH cirrhosis should consider the following for trial 131 design and efficacy endpoints: 132
candidates.context: B. Trial Design/Efficacy Endpoints 129 • Drugs for the treatment of compensated NASH cirrhosis should be evaluated in 134 randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trials. Sponsors can propose 135 stratification factors (e.g., T2DM, vitamin E, pioglitazone) and discuss with the FDA 136 before initiating phase 3 trials. 137

candidates.statement: Assessment of potential drug-related liver toxicity can be challenging in patients with chronic 169 liver disease. The FDA encourages the sponsor to develop a specific approach (e.g., an 170 algorithm) for monitoring liver function in patients with abnormal liver function at baseline, 171 including criteria for drug discontinuation for individual patients and trial stopping rules 172 (temporary or permanent). The protocol should specify guidelines for monitoring liver function. 173 The sponsor should establish an expert committee to adjudicate cases that meet protocol-defined 174
candidates.context: C. Safety Considerations 167 criteria for drug-induced liver injury. Given the growing evidence for an association between 175 NAFLD and cardiovascular disease, cardiovascular safety should be adequately monitored 176 during the clinical trial. 177
